title: Constant Pressure-controlled Extrusion Method for the Preparation of Nano-sized Lipid Vesicles
protocol: Retrieve a 20 mL glass vial with a Teflon-lined cap.
Clean all glassware and syringes with chloroform.
Transfer 100 μL of reagent grade chloroform to the glass vial using a 250 μL air-tight glass syringe.
Add 30 μL of reagent grade methanol to the same glass vial using a 100 μL air-tight glass syringe.
Transfer 216 μL of 10 mg/mL POPC solution in CHCl3 to the glass vial.
Transfer 42 μL of 10 mg/mL POPE solution in CHCl3 to the glass vial.
Transfer 20 μL of 11 mg/mL cholesterol solution in CHCl3 to the glass vial.
Evaporate the organic solvents using slow-flow argon or nitrogen gas until a thin film is observed on the bottom of the vial.
Place the uncapped glass vial in a vacuum desiccator for at least 30 minutes.
Transfer 2 mL of buffer, previously passed through a 0.2 micron filter, to the glass vial.
Incubate the mixture at 4 °C overnight and use within 48 hours.
Freeze liposome suspension in liquid nitrogen for 15 seconds.
Thaw liposome suspension using a heating block at 42 °C temperature for ~3 minutes.
Repeat steps 2.1 and 2.2 for a total of 5 cycles.
Follow the Avestin instructions to correctly assemble the Liposofast LF-50 extruder, using the instrument outline in their guide book.
Place the large hole support screen in the support filter base.
Follow by placing the circular sintered dish on top of the support screen.
Add one drain disc and one polycarbonate membrane, each with a diameter of 25 mm.
Secure the polycarbonate membrane to the support filter base using a small black O-ring.
Attach the top filter extruder to the support filter base by tightening 4 screws in corresponding holes.
Assemble the filter extruder unit underneath the large extruder barrel.
Add liposome solution to the cylinder barrel of the extruder.
Place the following components on top of the extrusion barrel in order: large circular O-ring, narrow cap, large circular O-ring, and circular cap.
Connect the gas regulator to the extruder barrel top.
Close all valves including the pressure relief valve to prevent air leakage.
Set up a 20 mL glass vial or 50 mL Erlenmeyer flask under the extruder filter unit for collection.
Attach a safety valve connected to the regulator, which will release if pressure exceeds 600 psi.
Turn on the nitrogen gas supply and open the gas valve connected to the extruder.
Increase nitrogen pressure to 25 psi for 400 nm liposomes.
Increase nitrogen pressure to 125 psi for 100 nm liposomes.
Increase nitrogen pressure to 400-500 psi for 30 nm liposomes.
Monitor the liposome suspension as it ejects into the container under pressure from the nitrogen gas.
Continue applying nitrogen until no liquid passes through the extruder filter.
Prepare 50 μL of a 20 μM liposome solution for Dynamic Light Scattering (DLS) analysis.
Turn on the power source and the lamp source.
Open the DynaPro software.
Set the software to the MS/X algorithm model to detect liposomes of 30 nm and 100 nm.
Set the software to the MS800 algorithm model to detect >100 nm liposomes.
Connect to the hardware.
Pipette 14 μL of liposome sample into the quartz cuvette.
Insert the cuvette into the cell holder.
Press start.
Press stop after ~20 - 30 acquisitions.
Analyze the average liposome diameter peaks recorded on the histogram.
Prepare a 500 μL, 0.1 μM liposome solution.
Rinse the sample compartment with water.
Rinse the sample compartment with ethanol.
Dry the sample compartment with a lint-free paper towel.
Turn on the laser power source and the computer.
Deliver 300 μL of 0.1 μM liposome solution to the sample compartment.
Open the Temperature control and the Nanoparticle Tracking Analysis software.
Press Capture button to turn on the laser.
Move the stage using horizontal and vertical adjustments.
Adjust the microscope focus.
Set the desired temperature (20 °C).
Set the recording time (at least 30 seconds).
Press the Record button to take multiple picture frames of the liposome particles for a specified amount of time.
Analyze the peaks corresponding to the diameter liposome sizes on the histogram as it tracks the motion of each particle.
Extrude hydrated liposomes of 2 mM through a polycarbonate 30 nm membrane at 500 psi with 5 passes.
Extrude hydrated liposomes through a 100 nm polycarbonate membrane at 125 psi with 5 passes.
Extrude hydrated liposomes through a 400 nm polycarbonate membrane at 25 psi with 2 passes.
